choices: It cannot be determined without a simulation
At least 10 heads, since that outcome includes 'exactly 10' plus many other successful counts
Exactly 10 heads, since 10 is the single most probable head-count in 20 flips

Three cards are in a hat: one is red on both sides, one is blue on both sides, and one is red on one side and blue on the other. You pick a card at random and look at one random side — it is red. What is the probability the other side of that same card is also red?
Consider the infinite series 1 − 1 + 1 − 1 + 1 − 1 + ⋯ (Grandi's series). Do its partial sums converge to a single value in the ordinary sense?
choices: No — the partial sums oscillate forever between 1 and 0, never settling on one value

Three prisoners each have a hat that is independently red or blue with 50% probability. Each can see the other two hats but not their own, and all three must simultaneously guess their own hat colour or pass. They win only if at least one guesses and everyone who guesses is correct. Using the optimal strategy — guess the opposite colour of what you see if the other two hats match, otherwise pass — what is their probability of winning?

A plane flies at a constant airspeed through a constant wind, from city A to city B and then straight back to city A along the same path. Compared to a completely windless day, does the round trip take the same time, more time, or less time?
choices: More time than on a windless day
Less time, because the average ground speed is higher
It depends on the wind's direction relative to the flight path
Exactly the same time, since the headwind and tailwind cancel out

choices: It cannot be done with only one draw
